messages:
support-cx: FYI customer C-172 reports a sharp p95/p99 latency jump when calling /v1/generate from APAC to our us-east region, started ~10:20 UTC. They attached traces and said DNS lookup time went from ~20ms to 220ms :grimacing:
sre-oncall: saw the alert too, p95 crossed 550ms for a 10m window. alert id: LAT-APAC-2958, linked graphs. :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: Incident LAT-APAC-2958 created and notified channel #pagerduty.
maya: can you paste the customer's traceroute and curl timings? any consistent hop that ballooned?
support-cx: pasted logs in ticket: "traceroute shows extra hop through ia-ldn-2 (AS 64512) then to us-east-gw, DNS resolving via our regional GSLB IPs with 200ms RTT occasionally"
eli: curious — did we just flip any GSLB routing weights earlier today? I remember a small rollout to change fallback region for apac last night.
net-eng: I rolled a tiny change at 03:10 PDT that adjusted health-weighting for apac -> us-east fallback (canary). Noticed a couple of probes failing then recovered. I'll pull the rollout diff.
own: running quick repro from singapore: ``time curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_namelookup} %{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate`` result: `0.212 0.045 0.520 0.708` (name lookup 212ms)
maya: that's consistent with customer. can you `dig +trace` against their resolver? also `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com +short`
own: `dig +trace` shows our GSLB returning a list with an anycast IP and a region-local IP. resolution path shows a delegation through a third-party CDN resolver that sometimes routes via london.
eli: that london detour explains the extra RTT. Did the rollout change health-checks so some APAC resolvers prefer the london hop?
net-eng: yes, the change reduced weight for apac-local pool when probes briefly flapped, so GSLB started returning the fallback candidate which routes via LDN POP for some resolvers.
maya: mitigation options: 1) revert health-weighting change (fast), 2) pin GSLB to prefer geo-local answers for APAC resolvers, 3) increase DNS TTL and rely on cached local answers (short-term?), 4) add an explicit emergency route for the affected customer region. Thoughts?
eli: I like revert first to stop ongoing harm. net-eng, can you rollback the canary immediately?
net-eng: rolling back now. command: ``gslb rollback --canary-id=cfg-2026-03-15-01``
sre-oncall: ping when rollback complete, we'll watch p95 graphs and customer repro.
(30s) net-eng: rollback finished. GSLB config now at previous stable.
deploy-bot: Rollback succeeded: cfg-2026-03-14-stable applied.
own: re-ran curl from sg: `0.018 0.040 0.150 0.210` name lookup 18ms — back to normal. :white_check_mark:
maya: looks good. can we verify across a sample of APAC resolvers and customer ASN?
eli: kicked off a distributed dig probe job (internal) across APAC probes and the customer's ASN. initial sweep shows 95% now resolve to apac-local anycast.
net-eng: we'll also add a short-term fix: increase apac pool probe threshold and add a suppression so transient probe failures don't flip weight for 5m. I'll open a follow-up RFC to revisit probe sensitivity.
maya: communications: support-cx please update the customer: explain root cause (GSLB fallback due to canary probe flip -> london detour increased DNS RTT -> p95 spike), actions taken (rollback, probe threshold change), and ETA for long-term fix.
support-cx: will send update now, include before/after curl numbers and offer a postmortem call.
eli: final notes for postmortem: include timeline (canary rollout time, probe failures, DNS delegate path change), sample traces, mtr/traceroute, `dig +trace`, and graphs for name-lookup latency. Also examine why our health probes flapped (network vs probe timeout).
sre-oncall: closing incident once we see 30m stable p95 under threshold; keeping channel open for any regressions.
net-eng: filing follow-up ticket RFC-2958-gslb-probe-sensitivity for permanent fix.
support-cx: customer confirmed latency normalized, will remain on-call for their tests. thanks all :pray:
maya: nice quick rollback. :tada:
(archive)
